What sort of creature are you, mortal, that comes stumbling to Sotha Sil, the Clockwork City of the Three-in-One? Are you of Nirn, or Oblivion, or one of the many realms besides? And how, I wonder, did you arrive? No matter. All shall reveal itself in time. You are here now, and in your shadow lurks the Prince of Plots. You will do nothing but foul and corrupt my works, though inadvertently, or else die unknown.
Be wary, mortal. I am not... fully in control, here. Everything is failing, it seems, and should that lift fail you will be beyond my assistance.
I feared that would happen. Mortal, there is an ancillary lift on the far side of the complex. Make your way there as quickly as you can. Stop for absolutely nothing. This floor is extremely unsta-

You thought you could fool me, didn't you? Fraudulent deceiver! The Dwemer are crafty, and seek ever to unbalance the perfect order of Resdayn! My advisors warned me. They said a look-alike would come, and here you are. You shall not survive!

Through that doorway is the Fabricant manufactory. It has been corrupted, and is completely beyond my control. I would advise you not to enter, as you would most likely be torn to pieces by rogue Fabricants.

So, you've chosen to disregard my advice and enter. Stupid of you. Very well, then. I shall channel your stupidity to a constructive end. I would have you repair this portion of the City. You must rebuild the two portions of the foundry, that which created life, and the other, which created machine.

Thank you, mortal, for aiding me in this endeavor. I had feared the permanent loss of my foundry, but you have exceeded my expectations and aided me considerably. Now you may come to the City proper, meet its citizenry, and rest. You are now a citizen of Sotha Sil for your exemplary service, as a formality, you should speak with the Archcanon. Should I have further need of you, you will know.
That, mortal, is the Imperfect. The Clockwork God was as vulnerable to imperfection as all else is, and so He created it, His finest work, as a monument to and grave of the faults He left behind.

It acted as his closest guardian, but it has gone mad, Imperfection given form without Perfection to restrain it. It is the being that has caused the ruin of my city, and I would have you kill him, mortal, though he deserves it not. He has acted from madness rather than malice, but he must be destroyed for the good of the City.

You are approaching the heart of this city, mortal, though it lies dark and empty. There is no movement, and it beats no longer. Make haste! Greater powers conspire against you, and malfunctions abound. Take care. It would be ill-suited for the hero to die just before their moment of triumph.

That, mortal, is the Imperfect. The Clockwork God was as vulnerable to imperfection as all else is, and so He created it, His finest work, as a monument to and grave of the faults He left behind. It acted as his closest guardian, but it has gone mad, Imperfection given form without Perfection to restrain it.

It is the being that has caused the ruin of my city, and I would have you destroy it, mortal, though he deserves it not. He has acted from madness rather than malice, but he must be destroyed for the good of the City.

The body is a wondrous mechanism, and so few bother to plumb its secrets. Even without the aid of magic, it can fight diseases on its own. But, what if the body itself becomes diseased? Why, it turns on itself. If you've ever seen a victim of Corprus, you know what horrors can result.
The corridors ahead are trap-laden, so I would advise you to remain on guard. If you die here, that will be all the proof I need that you would have been no use to me.

Oh, well done. You've managed to survive. Truly impressive. But, what are you, you ask me. I can hear the thought buzzing about you, nipping at the back of your mind. I am Gestalt, regent of the Clockwork City. I need no other name.

You survived the outer halls, and have exceeded my expectations in so doing. You have seen my city, and the state it languishes in. I would have you aid me, mortal, in repairing it. You arrived without my leave, so you may leave only under my sufferance.

This room might amuse you briefly, mortal. It contains an early experiment on fabricant fabrication, it's absolutely useless now, of course, but it never does to destroy one's own work, not when so much can be learned from mistakes.

It is a fundamental truth of our world that all things regress from the divine. These rooms and corridors, flooded, rusting, and decayed, provide all the proof of that axiom any mer could need. It is said that the Dwemer, in their folly, and the Altmer, in their arrogance, sought and seek to reverse this, the most constant of laws. In their sin, I am no different.

An impressive vista, is it not? A neverending font that keeps my City ticking away. There were two lighthouse keepers that kept vigil here, once, though I suppose that they, too, have been lost. So much is.

I've opened a path, flee!
A mark of wisdom is knowing when you're outmatched, and a mark of a survivor is awareness of one's surroundings.
Your constant flight causes me to question the wisdom of keeping you around. Nevertheless.
